note: Original educational scene copy; fictional mascot dialogue, not sacred text. Hebrew reviewed for grammar and niqqud; no blessings or divine names. Religious visuals are illustrative, not a practical halakhic ruling.

quips.ru: Есть место ещё для одного друга
quips.en: There's room for one more friend
A light breeze, a good book
The book is waiting for us
One more chair for the guests
Tonight we're reading in the sukkah

sceneGuidance: Courtyard preparation: timber, detached palm fronds, neatly stored tools, rolled wall fabric; no religious calendar/date claims.

Sukkah construction: stable walls before adding detached plant roofing; open sky above, no overhanging tree canopy, awning, or permanent roof; plant covering visually gives more shade than sunlight, with small gaps.

Decorating: colorful paper chains and fruit illustrations, preferably wall decorations to avoid unintended roofing implications. Decorative practice is common but not universal or required; do not present it as a universally observed ritual.
Welcoming guests: open entrance, extra chairs, cups and fruit; ordinary friends labeled guests. Do not identify fantasy mascot friends as the mystical ushpizin.
ReadingRoom: book and chair inside sukkah, schach visible overhead. Ordinary reading in a sukkah is a culturally grounded scene.
Mediatheque: side-wall screen inside sukkah on a fictional weekday Chol HaMoed evening. Do not call it a depiction of Shabbat/Yom Tov practice or a ritual.

Four species: one tall closed palm frond plus three myrtle sprigs and two willow sprigs, bound as one bundle; bumpy yellow citron remains separate. Myrtle leaves grouped in threes; willow leaves longer and narrower. Broad roof fronds are visually distinct from the ritual lulav.
Avoid Hanukkah menorahs, dreidels, faux sacred writing, blessings used as casual jokes, and claims that the scene establishes practical religious compliance.
